cookingOils.name: Extra Virgin Olive Oil (EVOO)
cookingOils.description: Dominated by oleic acid (18:1, monounsaturated) with minimal bis-allylic carbons. Rich in endogenous phenolic antioxidants (oleocanthal, hydroxytyrosol, tyrosol) that act as radical scavengers, terminating lipid peroxyl radical cascades and suppressing cytotoxic aldehyde formation despite moderate smoke point.

cookingOils.name: Refined Avocado Oil
cookingOils.description: Exceptional thermal ceiling with high monounsaturated oleic acid fraction. Extremely resilient against oxidative cleavage at temperatures up to 220°C. Minimal volatile secondary oxidation aldehydes under forced air convection.

cookingOils.name: High-Oleic Sunflower Oil
cookingOils.description: Selectively bred to reverse the standard sunflower fatty acid ratio, replacing fragile linoleic acid with 82% oleic acid. Lacks the vulnerability of standard sunflower oil, producing over 75% fewer cytotoxic alkenals during high-temperature frying.

cookingOils.name: Refined Canola (Rapeseed) Oil
cookingOils.description: Contains a high proportion of oleic acid, but its 9% alpha-linolenic acid (omega-3) and 19% linoleic acid (omega-6) make it susceptible to dual peroxidation pathways, forming both 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE) and 4-hydroxy-2-hexenal (4-HHE) when heated in convective air.

cookingOils.name: Refined Corn (Maize) Oil
cookingOils.description: High content of linoleic acid (18:2, omega-6) with abundant bis-allylic methylene carbons. Under turbulent air and heat, hydrogen abstraction triggers severe free radical propagation, generating heavy concentrations of toxic 4-HNE and conjugated dienes.

cookingOils.name: Refined Soybean Oil (Commercial Vegetable Oil)
cookingOils.description: The predominant commercial frying oil in fast food. High concentrations of both linoleic and linolenic acids create rapid peroxide accumulation and volatile aldehyde off-gassing. Degrades catastrophically when reused over multiple cycles.

cookingOils.name: Standard (Linoleic) Sunflower Oil
cookingOils.description: Contains nearly 70% linoleic acid. Produces the highest quantified yield of cytotoxic 4-HNE per gram of oil of any common culinary lipid when subjected to forced-air convective heat above 180°C.

cookingOils.name: Refined Peanut (Groundnut) Oil
cookingOils.description: Traditional deep-frying favorite with high heat tolerance and balanced oleic/linoleic profile. Resilient in submerged deep fryers, though its 32% linoleic fraction will progressively oxidize if subjected to air convection.

cookingOils.name: Refined Coconut Oil
cookingOils.description: Predominantly saturated medium-chain triglycerides (lauric, myristic). Completely devoid of bis-allylic carbons, rendering it virtually immune to thermal lipid peroxidation and 4-HNE formation, though high in saturated fat.

cookingOils.name: Clarified Butter (Ghee)
cookingOils.description: Milk solids (casein, lactose) removed by simmering and filtration. High saturated and monounsaturated content gives extreme resistance to oxidative cleavage, generating negligible toxic aldehydes even at 220°C.

cookingMethods.name: Forced-Air Convection (Air Fryer)
cookingMethods.description: High-velocity turbulent air sweeps continuously over a micro-thin oil film. While total oil consumed is reduced by 70%–85%, the dramatic oxygen mass transfer rate accelerates peroxide and aldehyde formation per gram of oil.

cookingMethods.name: Submerged Deep-Fat Fryer (Batch Oil Bath)
cookingMethods.oxygenExposure: Low at Food Surface (Protective steam vapor blanket; air only at bath surface)
cookingMethods.description: Food is fully immersed in an oil bath. Water boiling out of the food forms an escaping steam blanket that drives oxygen away from the food surface. However, food absorbs 3x to 5x more oil by mass, multiplying systemic aldehyde ingestion if oil is reused.

cookingMethods.name: Shallow Pan Frying (Skillet Sauté)
cookingMethods.oxygenExposure: Moderate (Upper food surface exposed to ambient air)
cookingMethods.description: Intermediate oil reservoir with conductive pan floor contact. Uneven heat distribution creates localized hot spots exceeding 220°C, accelerating thermal decomposition at pan boundaries.

cookingMethods.name: Standard Convection Oven Roasting
cookingMethods.oxygenExposure: Moderate-High (Large cavity, gentle fan air circulation)
cookingMethods.description: Moderate convective air movement over a larger baking sheet. Extended cooking dwell times (25–40 minutes) offset the lower air velocity, allowing cumulative thermal oxidation to progress.

reuseCycles.label: Cycle 1: Fresh Virgin Oil (First Use)
reuseCycles.description: Pristine oil structure. Free fatty acids and primary hydroperoxides are at factory baseline levels.

reuseCycles.label: Cycle 2–3: Light Reuse (Home Filtered)
reuseCycles.description: Primary oxidation products begin cleaving into secondary volatiles. Oil color slightly deepens.

reuseCycles.label: Cycle 4–5: Moderate Commercial Reuse
reuseCycles.description: Polymerization accelerates. Foaming tendencies increase and smoke point drops by 20°C–30°C.

reuseCycles.label: Cycle 6–8: Heavy Commercial Abuse (Exceeds EU TPC Limit)
reuseCycles.description: Exceeds the European statutory discard limit of 24%–25% Total Polar Compounds. High concentrations of cyclic fatty acid monomers, acrolein, and 4-HNE.

reuseCycles.label: Cycle 9+: Exhausted Rancid Oil (Hazardous)
reuseCycles.description: Severely degraded, viscous, dark oil. Hydroperoxides decompose rapidly into toxic aldehydes that penetrate deeply into food.

foodSubstrates.name: Cut Russet Potato French Fries
foodSubstrates.description: Porous cellular structure creates high specific surface area. Absorbs massive oil quantities during deep frying, but requires only a thin oil coating in air fryers.

foodSubstrates.name: Battered / Breaded Chicken Breast Nuggets
foodSubstrates.description: Flour and starch batter sponge absorbs large amounts of frying fat. Contains dietary free amino acids that accelerate Maillard reactions.

foodSubstrates.name: Breaded Mozzarella Sticks
foodSubstrates.description: High moisture and dairy fat core creates rapid steam expansion during frying, driving intense lipid exchange at the crumb barrier.

foodSubstrates.name: Vegetable Medley (Broccoli, Zucchini, Carrots)
foodSubstrates.description: High water release suppresses internal oil penetration. Natural plant antioxidant vitamins (vitamin C, carotenoids) provide slight protective buffering.

foodSubstrates.name: Salmon Fillet with Skin
foodSubstrates.description: Contains intrinsic marine long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA and DHA) that are themselves susceptible to thermal oxidation if cooked at excessive heat.
